p.i: Laudate eum testudine tinnula, Laudate plectris, omnibus organis, Clangore acuto buccinarum, Et lituis resonate curnis.
Sit iuncta fistro buxea fistula, Ἀμούσα passim & musica perstrepant, Cum barbitus nabla audiantur, Et tumidi quatiantur utres.
Omnes sonoris clangite cymbalis, Ductate folles cum crepitaculis, Fauces repurgate frequentent, Et digiti moveantur unci.
Quicunque puro vescitur æthere, Quicunque spirat, concelebret Deum. Laudate cælo præsidentem Qui nitidis dominatur astris.

IN Domino mihi certa salus: nil omnia vestrûm Verba moror, qui me fugere, & migrare monetis. Vt pauidus fugiens passerculus auolat alis. Ecce sed adductum iam contrahit impius arcum, Mittendásq; aptat nervo trepidante sagittas, Vt clandestino innocuum transfigat ab ictu. Ne qua tui vero tibi sit [?] fiducia iuris, Aspice convulso labefactas cardine leges, Fas versum atque nefas: ideoq; hoc tempore iustos

page.notes: Greek word in verse 4 (Ἀμούσα) is read from the scan and may be inaccurate; check against the page. "fit" in Ps. XI line 6 is doubtful (long s or f). "curnis" in verse 3 is read as printed and may be "cornis". "vestrûm" is read with a tilde over u. Verse lines are run together within each stanza; the printed line breaks are not kept. Verse numbers 3 to 6 stand in the left margin. The stanza "IN Domino..." begins with a large initial I, read as IN. The catchword "Quas" stands at bottom right, below the last line. Right edge shows show-through, not transcribed.
